case_name: Pandit Jhandu Lal and Others v State of Punjab and Others
facts: The appellants are the owners of agricultural land measuring about 86 bighas odd, in village Munda Majra, Tehsil Jagadhari, in the district of Ambala.

On October 27, 1954, the Additional District Magistrate of Ambala ordered the land to be requisitioned under the Punjab Requisitioning & Acquisition of Immoveable Property Act (XI of 1953) for the construction of houses by members of the Thapar Industries Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., Yamuna Nagar.
Possession of the land was taken on November 5, 1954.
The appellants instituted a suit on November 14, 1954, in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Jagadhari, challenging the requisition proceedings.

The trial Court dismissed the suit on June 25, 1956, on the preliminary ground that the suit was not competent in the absence of a previous notice under s. 59 of the Punjab Co-operative Societies Act, 1955 (XIV of 1955).

During the pendency of the civil litigation aforesaid, in spite of the fact that the second respondent had obtained delivery of possession through Government agency, by an Order of Injunction issued by the Court, construction had been stayed.

As soon as the High Court decided the suit in favour of the respondents, the second respondent 'started making huge constructions on the land in dispute in a very speedy manner', as alleged by the appellants in their petition under Art. 226 of the Constitution, which they filed on February 13, 1957.
issues: Whether or not the proceedings were vitiated by reason of the admitted fact that no proceedings under Part VII of the Act had been taken in making the acquisition
petitioner_arguments: The acquisition was by the Government for a public purpose, namely, of construction of tenements for industrial workers, under a scheme.
The restriction that the animal must be over 20 years of age and also unfit for work or breeding is an excessive or unreasonable restriction.
respondent_arguments: The proceedings were not vitiated by reason of the admitted fact that no proceedings under Part VII of the Act had been taken in making the acquisition.
The test laid down is not merely permanent incapacity or unfitness for work or breeding but the test is something more than that, a combination of age and unfitness.
court_reasoning: The restriction that the animal must be over 20 years of age and also unfit for work or breeding is an excessive or unreasonable restriction.
It seems to us that cl. (a) of sub-s. (2) of s. 4 of the Act as drafted is bad because it imposes a disproportionate restriction on the slaughter of bulls, bullocks and buffaloes.
holding: The appeal was allowed and the decision of the High Court was set aside.
The acquisition proceedings were held to be void for want of compliance with the procedure laid down in Chapter VII (mistake for Part VII) of the Act.
